object_description: low five-storey building with cantilevered upper volume
design_condition: Placed centrally on the property with a recessed base, the low volume creates four outdoor subspaces, a spacious street forecourt, and covered seating while maintaining the campus scale.

positive.statement: The low height references the existing campus buildings and makes the new building an equal player.
The recessed base expands the open space beneath the cantilevered building.
The interior presents a spatially appealing and rich inner world.
The closable two-story multi-purpose room expands the spaciousness of the public ground-floor zones.
The lateral staircases provide direct access and also serve as fire escapes.
The classrooms have good proportions and efficient divisibility.
The project achieves attractive build values through compact and resource-saving design.

negative.statement: The potential of the western square is not sufficiently exploited as a place to stay.
The northeast outdoor areas are likely to be shady and drafty, with unappealing furnishings.
The spacious forecourt lacks a clear design signature and an inviting entrance idea.
The floor plan is very introverted, with access to the outside only through the stairwells.
The sports halls lack daylight and their equipment-room arrangement is uneconomical.
The ventilation system and fixed sun-control elements are not functionally convincing.
The facades still show little identity.
The necessary sun protection is completely missing.
